note: Famous trees Commons has a category for and we do not map. Found by scripts/famous_trees.py; each one already has photographs and usually coordinates, so the expensive half of a research pass is done. Not verified by us, not published. Verified and written 2026-09-07: 4 candidates each passed the single-tree-destination test and shipped as new single-tree places under the 2026-08-31 exception, none within an existing city's walk radius: herchies (hrc_001, Chene a Clous), liernu (lie_001, Gros Chene), bioul (bio_001, Grand Tilleul), westerlo (wtl_001, Etagelinde). One (Allee de marronniers, Han-sur-Lesse) moved to blocked as an avenue rather than a single collectible point. List deduped (several names had been recorded twice). Second verification pass 2026-09-26 (verify agent, following BRIEF_RESEARCH.md): worked through all 14 remaining leads. 5 cleared the bar and were written to data/research/_famous-belgium-verified.json (lor_001 Caesarsboom, gos_002 Clawe Fawe, sht_001 Six Hetres de Longlou, wey_001 the Weywertz lime, stv_001 Antoniusbaum, the last two recommended HELD rather than shipped standalone; gos_002 recommended for integration into the existing Jalhay page rather than as a new place). 2 moved to blocked (Kapel- en etagelinde Nukerke: original tree confirmed dead, felled by storm 2019; Zilverlinde bij het Blindenhuis Gent: confirmed inside a private walled institutional garden). 5 remain leads with a clear why (Groene Beuk, Chene seculaire Hamerenne, the Volkershouw oak, Koningslinde, Tilleul de Miermont, Opgaande fladderiep) -- see each entry. If de la decapitation's stray lead-array status synced to match its existing blocked-array entry.

leads.name: Antoniusbaum (Sankt-Vith)
leads.verify_progress: 2026-09-07 partial check: protected as landscape of the German-speaking Community of Belgium since 10-10-1985 (Wikidata Q57352818 and the English/Dutch Wikipedia lists of protected heritage sites in Sankt-Vith both confirm the designation and give a precise Wikidata coordinate, used here). Neither source gives species, age, girth or any story/folklore beyond the name (Antonius = Saint Anthony, so likely a devotional tree similar in kind to Herchies' chene a clous, but that is inference, not sourced). No news coverage or visitor-destination evidence found in the time available. Needs: species, age/girth, and evidence of why anyone would seek it out specifically (a local history source or the 'Unsere Gemeinde' municipal newsletter PDF at st.vith.be may have this, not fetched this pass). Does not currently pass the destination test on available evidence; a from-scratch pass with more time on ostbelgienkulturerbe.be (the region's own heritage database, linked from the Wikipedia entry) could change that.
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 second pass: confirmed on file (existence, protection date, coordinate) via the same heritage register plus one new independent source, GrenzEcho (a regional newspaper, 2007, paywalled beyond the teaser but confirming the site is a real, actively-visited, tended hiking destination). Still no species or age anywhere. Recommend HOLD rather than publish standalone: no distinguishing fact beyond a devotional statue. Written up in full in the verified file as a seed for a possible future small Sankt-Vith/German-speaking Community cluster page, paired with the Weywertz lime (stv_001 / wey_001 in that file).

leads.name: Clawé faw
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 verification pass: real and distinct from our already-published gos_001 (Les Sept Freres de Gospinal, a multi-trunk oak roughly 100-150m away in the same patch of forest). This is 'Clawe Fawe', a beech 'nail tree' (arbre a clous) in the Bois de Foyr near Jalhay, girth 379cm (2013), a genuine local folk-medicine and boundary-marker/gibbet-site tradition, confirmed by fr.wikipedia's 'Arbre a clous' article and mini-ardenne.be's tourism page. No age found. IMPORTANT: the 'fame' field currently on our published gos_001 wrongly links it to this tree's Wikidata item (Q13495179) by coordinate proximity; that link should be corrected, it is not evidence the two are the same tree. Recommend this join the existing Jalhay city page as a second stop (proposed id gos_002) rather than ship as a new standalone place, since it is a short walk from gos_001 in the same commune.

leads.name: Groene Beuk (Hof ter Saksen)
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: existence and rough notability confirmed by exactly one real source, Dutch Wikipedia's 'Hof ter Saksen' article, which names 'een oude groene beuk' (an old green beech) among the arboretum's most valuable trees; a gallery caption independently calls it 'monumentale groen beuk'. That is arguably one source republished twice rather than two independent ones. No girth, no age, and no tree-level coordinate found anywhere (monumentaltrees.com's page for this arboretum 403'd to automated fetch, and plantaardigheden.nl's page returned no usable content). Hof ter Saksen itself is a genuine public, municipally-owned 27ha arboretum/park (Haasdonkbaan 101, Beveren), so ACCESS is not the problem here, sourcing depth is. What would unblock it: the specific onroerenderfgoed.be object number for this individual tree (a 'Kasteeldreef met opgaande bruine beuken' avenue entry exists for a DIFFERENT, ensemble of copper beeches on the same site, object 303074, and should not be confused with this one), or a monumentaltrees.com single-page browser fetch (hard rule 1 allows verification-only use).

leads.name: Six hêtres de Longlou
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 verification pass: real, classified since 1936 (Wallonia heritage register 63049-CLT-0003-01, via en.wikipedia's list of protected heritage sites in Malmedy), a beech clearing in the Fagne de Longlou near Beverce, historically a shepherds' resting place. Second independent source (komoot.com, directly fetched) confirms the age (~250 years) and, importantly, that the beeches are 'at the end of their life cycle' with young replacement saplings planted alongside them in 1993. An unconfirmed search-engine summary suggested only three of the six originals now survive; could not verify this on any page actually fetched, so it is NOT stated as fact, only flagged as a thing a future pass should check on the ground or via a recent photo. Recommend HOLD as a lead for a future Hautes Fagnes/Malmedy cluster rather than shipping alone, given the declining condition and the unresolved current tree count.

leads.name: Caesarsboom
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 verification pass: strongly corroborated, two independent sources (Flanders heritage inventory + English Wikipedia's dedicated article), both agreeing the true age is ~250 years despite a local legend claiming Julius Caesar tied his horse here 2000+ years ago (both sources call the legend folklore). Girth 250cm, height 7.5m, protected national monument since 2005, stands beside Lo's last surviving medieval town gate. Recommend SHIP as its own standalone place under the single-tree exception: real fame, a debunked-but-tellable legend, solid measurements, one obvious place to stand.

leads.name: If de la décapitation, Braine-le-Château
leads.verify_note: Status synced 2026-09-26 to match this lead's own full entry already present in this file's top-level 'blocked' list: verified real and alive (yew planted 1568) but the park is confirmed private, opening only for rare special events rather than as a standing bookable tour. See the 'blocked' array below for the full reasoning; not re-researched this pass.

leads.name: Chêne séculaire (Hamerenne)
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: no independent source beyond the bare Commons category found despite several search attempts (general web search, Wallonia arbres-remarquables search, fr.wikipedia's list of remarkable trees in Belgium, which covers other Namur-province villages like Liernu and Han-sur-Lesse but has no Hamerenne or Wanlin entry). Hamerenne is a hamlet of Rochefort, Namur province. What would unblock it: Wallonia's own AHREM/WalOnMap remarkable-trees geoportal (JS-rendered, not reachable by a plain text-search or curl fetch in this pass) or the DNF's remarkable-trees census searched by commune rather than by tree name. Left as a lead rather than blocked, since nothing found suggests a problem with the tree itself, only a gap in what this pass could reach.

leads.name: Opgaande eik bij oude kleiwinning (Volkershouw, Wetteren)
leads.species_basis: confirmed via Flanders heritage inventory, object 132085
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: the tree itself is well documented by one source, Flanders' heritage inventory (object 132085): a heavily developed Quercus robur, girth 360cm, height 25m (7m clear trunk), crown 26m, standing as a corner tree marking an old property boundary near a former clay pit, at Volkershouw 20, Westrem (Wetteren). Only one source found; more importantly, ACCESS could not be settled: the address reads as an ordinary residential street number and no source states whether the tree stands on the road verge (public) or inside the private plot (not). Per hard rule 10, left as a lead rather than published on a guess; a next pass should try the OSM/Overpass access-tag technique (BRIEF_RESEARCH.md, 'Settling access from OpenStreetMap') on Volkershouw before deciding either way.

leads.name: Koningslinde (Knokke-Heist)
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: the SQUARE (Tijl- en Neleplein, formerly Keuvelhoekplein) and its 1952 Tijl-and-Nele statue by Charles Samuel are well documented (nl.wikipedia's general 'Koningslinde' article on the cultivar/tradition, and a Zwinstreek heemkunde article on the statue's history), but nothing found independently dates, measures or otherwise distinguishes THIS specific linden; the name itself only comes from the Commons file titles. 'Koningslinde' is a generic Dutch name for a lime planted to mark a change of monarch (the cultivar Tilia europaea 'Pallida', first used this way for Queen Wilhelmina's 1898 coronation in the Netherlands), so this may well be a 20th-century commemorative planting rather than anything ancient; without a source naming the occasion this is a guess, not recorded. What would unblock it: a Knokke-Heist heemkring (local history society) piece or a municipal planting record naming this specific tree and its occasion.

leads.name: Linde (Weywertz)
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 verification pass: strongly corroborated, two independent sources (de.wikipedia's 'Weywertz' article and butgenbach.info's tourism page) agreeing on everything: planted 1668 (~358 years old), ~20m tall, protected as a Naturdenkmal since 1984, standing on the public square in front of St. Michael's church. Only genus given (Tilia), not species. Recommend considering it together with the Antoniusbaum lead (stv_001, also this pass, also German-speaking Community) for a possible small future cluster page; see the verified file for both.

leads.name: Kapel- en etagelinde (Nukerke)
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: CONFIRMED DEAD. This centuries-old 'etagelinde' (a linden trained in tiers, beside a chapel at a footpath crossroads south of Nukerke, Maarkedal) was felled by Storm Miguel in June 2019 (pers.oost-vlaanderen.be, a Flemish provincial press release, directly fetched). The province grafted cuttings from it before it was lost; a genetic descendant was planted 5 December 2024, but at a DIFFERENT chapel entirely (Our Lady of Seven Sorrows, Molenstraat, Kluisbergen), not at the original Nukerke crossroads. Nothing living currently stands at the mapped Nukerke site as far as this pass could establish. Moved to blocked per the never-doen-aan-dode-bomen rule; the Commons photos on this lead are historical record of a tree that no longer stands and must not be presented as current.

leads.name: Tilleul de Miermont
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: one real source found and directly fetched, saive.be's own hamlet-history page for Miermont, which places the tree at the crossroads of the rue sur Miermont and a path to Evegnee, the highest point of the plateau (boundary of Retinne/Saive/Evegnee-Tignee), appearing already on 18th-century maps, sheltering a wayside crucifix ('li Vi Bon d'Ju') that volunteers maintain, and noting it has been struck by lightning in the past. A search-engine summary separately claimed the tree is 400 years old and that a named lord administered justice under it; NEITHER detail could be confirmed on the fetched page itself, so per the search-summary caution rule neither is recorded as fact here. No coordinate was found anywhere for the crossroads itself (only the general Saive/Blegny area), and inventing one would be exactly the kind of faked precision this project forbids, so this stays a lead purely on that gap rather than on the tree's reality, which is not in doubt. What would unblock it: an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim lookup of 'rue sur Miermont' crossed with the path to Evegnee (not reachable with the tools available this pass), or Wallonia's AHREM geoportal entry if one exists for it.

leads.name: Opgaande fladderiep (Maelbroekstraat 45, Wetteren)
leads.species_basis: 'fladderiep' has only one common meaning in Dutch (Ulmus laevis); confirmed as a real Flanders heritage-inventory entry via its own beeldbank image record
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: existence and address confirmed via Flanders' own heritage image bank (beeldbank.onroerenderfgoed.be/images/190123, caption 'Maelbroekstraat 45. Opgaande Fladderiep'), which links to erfgoedobject 131220, but that object's own detail page returned a server error on every attempt this pass ('Er ging iets mis bij het ophalen van het gekoppelde erfgoed'), so no girth, age or precise coordinate could be pulled from it. IMPORTANT CORRECTION AVOIDED: an earlier search surfaced a fladderiep with a 3.15m girth described as the thickest known in East Flanders, but that figure belongs to a DIFFERENT, unrelated register entry (object 131478, Oud-Moregembos near Wortegem-Petegem) and must not be bridged onto this tree. Ulmus laevis is itself one of Flanders' rarest native trees (only a handful of known East-Flanders locations per that same unrelated entry's description), which is a fact about the species and a reason this specimen is worth pursuing, not a fact about this individual tree's size. No coordinate found for the address either; left as a lead on that gap. What would unblock it: retrying erfgoedobjecten/131220 once the site's error clears, or id.erfgoed.net's alternate URL form.

leads.name: Zilverlinde bij het Blindenhuis (Gent)
leads.species_basis: confirmed via Flanders heritage inventory, object 132468
leads.verify_note: 2026-09-26 pass: BLOCKED on access, not on the tree's reality. Flanders' heritage inventory (erfgoedobject 132468, directly fetched) confirms this monumental silver linden and states plainly it stands 'within the walled garden' on the eastern side of the former Blindenhuis Van Caeneghemgesticht, Coupure 65-55, Gent (protected urban landscape since 17 October 1980). No evidence of public access to that garden was found; the institution's public-facing successor (Licht en Liefde/vlaamsoogpunt Gent) has relocated to Kortrijksesteenweg 304, and nothing suggests the Coupure courtyard itself is open to visitors. See the full reasoning in this file's 'blocked' array. Would reopen on evidence the garden holds open days or public hours.

blocked.name: Allée de marronniers (Han-sur-Lesse)
blocked.reason: Ensemble is an avenue of horse chestnuts (allee), not one collectible point: CLAUDE.md/BRIEF_RESEARCH.md block avenues and whole woods outright regardless of fame or age. No single tree to stand at.

blocked.name: If de la décapitation, Braine-le-Château
blocked.reason: Verified as real and alive (yew planted 1568 in the chateau park, per fr.wikipedia list, TVcom local news 2022 and the Royal Syndicat d'Initiative de Braine-le-Château's own brochure) but the park is confirmed PRIVATE: pajawa.be states plainly it is "exceptionally accessible during occasional activities" organised by the local tourism syndicate, no free visits, guided tours only, reservation mandatory, and the one documented opening was a single weekend (2020-10-10/11). This is not a standing bookable tour (unlike the Menorca boat exception) but a rare special-event opening, so it fails the genuinely-open test under hard rule 10. Leave as a lead; revisit if the syndicate starts running it as a regular ticketed visit.

blocked.name: Remarkable Lime of Chantemelle
blocked.reason: Verified and written (species undated, no girth, no folklore, no story beyond Wallonia's bare heritage classification 85009-CLT-0008-01), but Chantemelle is not near any published city and the tree does not pass the single-famous-tree destination test ('would somebody travel specifically for THIS ONE TREE', CLAUDE.md 2026-08-31): a classified square-tree with no distinguishing fact is a fine village lime, not a destination. Held rather than published as its own place. Full verified record (sources, coordinates, written story) sits in git history of data/research/famousbelgium-verified.json, commit 9c29a659 and the write-pass commit that followed it, if a later pass finds a fact that changes the verdict.

blocked.name: Kapel- en etagelinde (Nukerke)
blocked.reason: Confirmed dead: the historic tiered linden at this chapel-and-crossroads site south of Nukerke (Maarkedal) was felled by Storm Miguel in June 2019 (pers.oost-vlaanderen.be press release, directly fetched 2026-09-26). A genetic graft descendant was planted 5 December 2024, but at a different chapel in Kluisbergen, not at this site. No living tree currently stands at the mapped location as far as this pass could establish.

blocked.name: Zilverlinde bij het Blindenhuis (Gent)
blocked.reason: Flanders' heritage inventory (erfgoedobject 132468, directly fetched 2026-09-26) states plainly this monumental silver linden (Tilia tomentosa) stands 'within the walled garden' on the eastern side of the former Blindenhuis Van Caeneghemgesticht at Coupure 65-55, Gent. No evidence of public access to that garden was found (the institution's own successor, Licht en Liefde/vlaamsoogpunt Gent, has since relocated its public-facing centre to Kortrijksesteenweg 304); the Coupure building's garden reads as a private institutional courtyard rather than open ground. Blocked under hard rule 10 pending evidence the garden is genuinely open to visitors.
